title: Box Truck Log App (Frontend) — Role-Based Dashboards, Logs, Documents, Questions

requirements.summary: Add Internet Identity sign-in gating and role-aware UI/route access for Admin vs User scopes.
acceptanceCriteria: Unauthenticated visitors are prompted to sign in with Internet Identity.
After sign-in, the UI clearly indicates whether the signed-in user is Admin or User.
User-only views do not show other users’ content.
Admin views can list and open content created by any user.
Backend enforces authorization checks (not only the UI).

file_operations.description: Create the app shell that gates all protected content behind Internet Identity, fetches caller role (via backend getCallerUserRole/isCallerAdmin), and conditionally renders Admin vs User experiences. Use the authorization component patterns for RBAC UI expectations; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Add role-aware route definitions for Admin and User sections and a default post-login redirect based on role. Include route guards that block non-admin access to admin views. Use the authorization component patterns for AccessDenied behavior; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Create an auth gate wrapper that prompts login when unauthenticated and blocks rendering of application data until identity is available. Use the authorization component patterns for login gating; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Create an admin-only wrapper that checks the caller role and either renders children or shows an authorization error screen (or redirects). Use the authorization component patterns for admin-only UX; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Implement first-login profile setup (ask for display name) using backend getCallerUserProfile/saveCallerUserProfile, ensuring it does not flash while the actor/queries load. Use the authorization component guidance for profile setup flow; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Add a header that shows app identity, the signed-in user's profile name, their role (Admin/User), and a login/logout control. Use the authorization component patterns for logout cache clearing; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Create React Query hooks to load current user profile + role (and admin boolean) from the backend actor, and expose a single derived 'auth state' for the app. Use the authorization component guidance for actor-dependent queries; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.
Wire the new router/app shell into the existing React entry so auth gating and role-based navigation apply to all screens.

requirements.summary: Implement Truck Logs UI: create/view/edit/delete for the signed-in user's entries, and admin read-only aggregate browsing across users.
acceptanceCriteria: A signed-in user can create a new log entry and see it appear in their log list.
A signed-in user can edit and delete their own log entries.
A signed-in user cannot edit/delete log entries belonging to another user.
An admin can view an aggregate list of all log entries and filter/group by user.
Log entries persist across page refreshes.

file_operations.description: Add React Query hooks for fetching caller logs and (admin-only) fetching all users’ logs, plus mutations for create/update/delete that invalidate the relevant queries on success.

Create the User 'My Logs' view with a responsive list/table, a create form (date/time display, optional title, notes, optional mileage), and edit/delete actions limited to the caller’s own entries using backend log functions.

Create the Admin 'All Logs' view that shows an aggregate list grouped/filterable by user (using user profile names when available) and supports opening an entry for viewing. Ensure no admin-only editing is implied unless supported; keep admin behavior read/browse per requirement.

Create a reusable log entry form component used by My Logs create/edit flows, with consistent validation and styling using existing UI primitives (do not modify immutable ui components; compose them instead).

Create a reusable, responsive list/table component for log entries with consistent empty/loading/error states using composed UI primitives (do not modify immutable ui components; compose them instead).
Register routes for My Logs (user scope) and All Logs (admin scope) and ensure navigation targets resolve correctly.

requirements.summary: Implement Documents UI: upload with metadata, list, and download/view for caller; admin browsing across all users.
acceptanceCriteria: User can upload a document and see it listed with filename, size, and upload time.
User can download/view a previously uploaded document.
Admin can browse documents across all users and download them.
Backend stores document metadata and bytes and returns correct bytes on download.
UI shows a clear error for disallowed/oversized uploads, and the upload does not partially persist.

file_operations.description: Add React Query hooks for fetching caller uploads and (admin-only) all uploads, plus a mutation for uploading a document that reports progress and handles backend errors cleanly. Use the blob-storage component concepts for ExternalBlob and progress tracking; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Create the User 'My Documents' view with an upload panel (file picker + content type/size handling) and a list showing filename, size, timestamp, plus actions to view/download via the stored blob reference. Use blob-storage ExternalBlob.getDirectURL()/getBytes appropriately; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Create the Admin 'All Documents' view that browses uploads across users (group/filter by user) and provides view/download actions. Use blob-storage ExternalBlob capabilities for efficient retrieval; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Create a composed upload UI (button/drag-drop if desired) that validates allowed/oversized files and displays upload progress. Use blob-storage ExternalBlob.withUploadProgress for progress UX; verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.
Create a reusable documents list/table component with consistent metadata display and view/download actions using composed UI primitives (do not modify immutable ui components; compose them instead).
Register routes for My Documents (user scope) and All Documents (admin scope) and ensure navigation targets resolve correctly.

requirements.summary: Implement Questions UI: user submit + list; admin browse all, set status (Open/Answered), and optionally reply.
acceptanceCriteria: User can submit a question and see it listed in their questions view.
Admin can see all users’ questions in an admin view.
Admin can change a question’s status (Open/Answered) and the change persists.
If admin replies are enabled, a user can see the admin reply for their question.
Backend prevents non-admins from changing other users’ question status/replies.

file_operations.description: Add React Query hooks for fetching caller questions and (admin-only) all questions, plus mutations for submit, update status, and admin reply, with proper invalidation and friendly handling of authorization failures.
Create the User 'My Questions' view with a submit form (question text) and a list showing timestamp, status, and admin reply when present.
Create the Admin 'All Questions' view that shows questions across users (group/filter by user), allows changing status (Open/Answered), and provides an optional reply editor to answer questions.
Create a reusable submit form component with consistent validation and styling using composed UI primitives (do not modify immutable ui components; compose them instead).

Create a reusable questions list/table component supporting both user and admin modes (admin controls for status/reply) using composed UI primitives (do not modify immutable ui components; compose them instead).
Register routes for My Questions (user scope) and All Questions (admin scope) and ensure navigation targets resolve correctly.

requirements.summary: Create Admin and User dashboards with navigation among Logs, Documents, and Questions, enforcing role scope and guarding admin routes.
acceptanceCriteria: After sign-in, users land on a dashboard appropriate to their role.
Navigation allows switching between Logs, Documents, and Questions within the role’s permitted scope.
Admin dashboard includes at least: All Logs, All Documents, All Questions views.
User dashboard includes at least: My Logs, My Documents, My Questions views.
Attempting to access admin routes/views as a non-admin redirects or shows an authorization error.

file_operations.description: Create a User dashboard layout ('users log') with shared navigation to My Logs, My Documents, My Questions, and an area for nested content; keep the scope strictly to caller-owned data.
Create an Admin dashboard layout ('admin log') with navigation to All Logs, All Documents, All Questions, plus lightweight overview counts/summary sections backed by existing queries.
Implement a role-aware navigation component used by both dashboards to present only permitted links and indicate the active section.
Wire nested dashboard routes so that post-login redirects land on the correct role dashboard, and unauthorized admin access is blocked via RequireAdmin.
Connect header + dashboards + routing so the app consistently routes to the appropriate role dashboard after authentication and profile setup.

requirements.summary: Apply a consistent fleet/truck-ops visual theme (non-blue/purple primary) across layouts, lists/tables, and forms; ensure responsive UX.
acceptanceCriteria: All primary pages share a consistent layout, typography, and color system.
Forms, buttons, and lists/tables use consistent variants and spacing.
The theme is not dominated by blue/purple as primary branding colors.
The UI is usable on mobile and desktop (responsive layout for dashboards and lists).

file_operations.description: Define the app’s global theme tokens (CSS variables used by Tailwind/shadcn styling) using a truck-ops palette (e.g., charcoal/graphite + safety orange + muted neutrals/greens) and apply consistent base typography/spacing defaults.
Adjust Tailwind theme extensions (if needed) to support the chosen non-blue/purple brand palette and consistent component radii/shadows for a rugged operations aesthetic.
Create a shared responsive page shell (content max width, padding, section headers) used across dashboards and primary pages to enforce consistent layout and spacing.

Create a consistent section header component (title/subtitle/actions slot) to standardize page headings for logs/documents/questions using composed UI primitives (do not modify immutable ui components; compose them instead).

requirements.summary: Add the required generated truck image asset and display it in the UI as a static frontend asset.
acceptanceCriteria: Generated image files exist under frontend/public/assets/generated with the exact filenames specified in imageRequirements.required.
At least one primary screen (e.g., header or landing/dashboard) displays the generated image.
No backend endpoints are used to serve the generated static image assets.

file_operations.description: Add the generated static image asset file at the exact required path: frontend/public/assets/generated/truck-logo.dim_512x512.png.
Display the generated truck logo image (frontend/public/assets/generated/truck-logo.dim_512x512.png) in a primary UI location such as the app header and/or dashboard header.
